after: A loop's `else` part runs when the loop finishes normally, even when there are no items to visit. It does not run if `break` leaves the loop. A `return` or an error that leaves the loop also skips this part.

This `else` belongs to the loop. It does not belong to an `if` inside that loop.

A search can use `break` when it finds a match. Then `else` can handle the case where no match was found.

`continue` skips the rest of one repeat. The loop can still finish normally and run its `else` part.

`contains_even` reads whole numbers from something you can loop over, such as a list. It checks whether any number is even and leaves the input unchanged.

If it finds an even number, `break` ends the loop. If the loop finishes without a match, `else` returns `False`.

